newsitem.title: USA: HSBC'S Midland unit says to cut 55 jobs.
newsitem.headline: HSBC'S Midland unit says to cut 55 jobs.

text.p: HSBC Holdings Plc unit HSBC Midland said on Friday it will cut 25 trader and assistant trader positions and 30 operation and finance positions from its New York foreign exchange department.
HSBC Midland also said interbank foreign exchange market making in New York will cease effective October 7.
Price making and processing will be centralized in the firm's London office, the firm said, with hours there expanded to serve clients throughout the U.S. trading day.

"HSBC Midland is widely regarded as one of the world's leaders in foreign exchange. We regret the redundancies that will result from these improvements, but we are confident that our customers will benefit from service enhancements afforded us by the establishment by the U.S. sales team of a virtual presence in our London dealing room, which is the largest in Europe," said Tony Rademeyer, HSBC Treasurer in New York.
HSBC Holdings plc said it is one of the world's largest banking and financial services organizations, with assets of over $368 billion at June 30, 1996 and offices in 75 countries.
